t.6.87.1: Seeing the two rākṣasas Mahodara and Mahāpārśva slain, and that mighty hero Virūpākṣa also struck down,
t.6.87.2: Then in that great battle a mighty rage took hold of Rāvaṇa; he urged on his charioteer and spoke these words.
t.6.87.3: By slaying those two, Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa, I myself shall remove the sorrow of the slain ministers and of the besieged city.
t.6.87.4: In battle I shall strike down the tree that is Rāma, which yields Sītā as its flower and fruit, and whose spreading branches are Sugrīva, Jāmbavān, Kumuda and Nala.
t.6.87.5: That great atiratha, making the ten directions resound with the roar of his chariot, set forth swiftly and advanced upon Rāghava.
t.6.87.6: Filled with that sound, the whole earth, with its rivers, mountains and forests, with its boars, deer and elephants, shook violently.
t.6.87.7: He discharged the Tāmasa weapon, exceedingly terrible and most dreadful, and burned up all the monkeys, who fell down on every side.
t.6.87.8: Seeing those many divisions broken by the hundreds by Rāvaṇa's excellent arrows, Rāghava stood firm, ready for battle.
t.6.87.9: Then he saw Rāma, the unconquered, standing together with his brother Lakṣmaṇa, like Vāsava standing with Viṣṇu.
t.6.87.10: Him, who, bracing his mighty bow, seemed to scrape the very sky: the long-armed tamer of foes, with large eyes like lotus petals.
t.6.87.11: Seeing the monkeys routed in battle and Rāvaṇa rushing toward him, Rāghava, filled with delight, grasped his bow by the middle.
t.6.87.12: Then he began to twang his excellent bow, of mighty force and mighty roar, as though splitting open the earth.
t.6.87.13: Having come within the range of the arrows of those two princes, Rāvaṇa became like Rāhu in the vicinity of the moon and the sun.
t.6.87.14: Then, because of Rāvaṇa's floods of arrows and that sound of the bow twanged by Rāma, the rākṣasas fell down by the hundreds.
t.6.87.15: Wishing to be the first to fight him with sharp arrows, Lakṣmaṇa drew his bow and released arrows that were like flames of fire.
t.6.87.16: Those arrows, the moment they were released by the bowman Lakṣmaṇa, the greatly glorious Rāvaṇa warded off in the sky with arrows of his own.
t.6.87.18: Passing beyond Saumitri, Rāvaṇa, victorious in battle, then approached Rāma, who stood immovable like a mountain.
t.6.87.17: Displaying the swiftness of his hand, he cut down Lakṣmaṇa's arrows, one with a single arrow, three with three, and ten with ten.
t.6.87.19: Having encountered Rāma in battle, Rāvaṇa, his eyes red with rage, loosed showers of arrows upon Rāghava.
t.6.87.20: Then Rāma, merely seeing the streams of arrows loosed from Rāvaṇa's bow swiftly falling upon him, quickly seized his crescent-headed bhalla shafts.
t.6.87.21: Then Rāghava, with sharp bhalla arrows, cut down those floods of arrows, blazing and of great speed, like enraged venomous serpents.
t.6.87.22: Swiftly Rāghava rained upon Rāvaṇa, and likewise Rāvaṇa upon Rāghava; the two showered each other with sharp arrows of many kinds.
t.6.87.23: Watching closely the onrush of the arrows, the two warriors, never vanquished in battles, moved for a long time in wondrous circles, now to the left and now to the right.
t.6.87.24: As those two fierce warriors fought together at the same time, loosing arrows and resembling Yama and Antaka, all beings trembled with fear.
t.6.87.25: Then the sky became covered with arrows of many kinds, as it is with clouds wreathed in garlands of lightning when the hot season has passed.
t.6.87.26: The sky became as if latticed with showers of arrows, swift and of great velocity, their points exceedingly sharp, well feathered with vulture plumes.
t.6.87.27: Then those two, like two great clouds risen up when the sun has gone to its setting, created a supreme and terrible darkness of arrows.
t.6.87.29: For both were supreme archers, both were skilled in weapons, and both were foremost among those versed in missiles; both ranged about in the battle.
t.6.87.28: A tumultuous battle broke out between the two, each eager to slay the other, a battle unapproachable and inconceivable, like that between Vṛtra and Vāsava.
t.6.87.30: For wherever the two of them moved, there the waves of arrows went, like the waves of two oceans driven by the wind.
t.6.87.31: Then Rāvaṇa, who makes the worlds cry out, his hands busily engaged, fastened a garland of iron arrows upon Rāma's forehead.
t.6.87.33: Then Rāma, filled with wrath, muttering incantations and invoking the fierce weapon of Rudra, took up arrows once more.
t.6.87.32: Bearing on his head that garland of arrows, loosed from the fierce bow and glowing like the petals of blue lotuses, Rāma felt no pain.
t.6.87.34: The mighty and greatly splendid one drew his bow and released them; having snatched up his arrows, he hurled those shafts at the lord of the rākṣasas.
t.6.87.36: Then once again Rāma, skilled in all weapons, pierced that lord of the rākṣasas, standing in his chariot, on the forehead with a supreme missile.
t.6.87.35: Those arrows, falling then upon the impenetrable armor of the lord of the Rākṣasas, which resembled a great cloud, caused him no distress.
t.6.87.37: Thwarted by Rāvaṇa, those arrows, like five-headed serpents, pierced through the arrow-shaped forms and, hissing, entered the earth.
t.6.87.38: Having struck down the missile of Rāghava, Rāvaṇa, stupefied with rage, took up another missile, an Āsura weapon exceedingly great and terrible.
t.6.87.39: And others with the faces of lions and tigers, with the faces of herons and crows, with the faces of vultures and hawks, and likewise with the faces of jackals.
t.6.87.41: He loosed arrows, some with the faces of donkeys and others shaped with the faces of boars, some with the mouths of dogs and cocks, and others with the jaws of crocodiles and venomous serpents.
t.6.87.40: He also loosed other sharp arrows bearing the faces of wolves, with gaping mouths and fearsome to behold, and others shaped like lions and like licking serpents.
t.6.87.42: Through his magic powers, the mighty one, enraged and hissing like a serpent, loosed these and other sharpened arrows at Rāma.
t.6.87.43: Assailed by that Āsura weapon, Raghunandana, of great vigour and like fire himself, discharged the weapon of Pāvaka.
t.6.87.44: He discharged arrows whose heads blazed like fire, arrows with heads like the sun, arrows with heads shaped like the moon and the half-moon, and arrows with heads like a comet.
t.6.87.45: He loosed sharp arrows, some bright as planets and stars, with tips like great meteors, and others resembling tongues of lightning.
t.6.87.46: Those terrible arrows of Rāvaṇa, struck down by the missiles of Rāghava, met their destruction in the sky, and they perished by the thousands.
t.6.87.47: Seeing that missile destroyed by Rāma, whose deeds are accomplished without strain, all the monkeys, able to take any form at will, then roared with delight.
